newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Wertheimers buy IDB's Iscar stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Wertheimers buy IDB's Iscar stake.

text.p: The Wertheimer family of Israel bought IDB Holding Corp's 26.7 percent stake in the privately held Iscar Ltd for $197 million in IDB shares and cash, Iscar chief financial officer Dany Goldman said on Sunday.
The purchase ends a long-running dispute between two of Israel's most powerful families over the publication of Iscar's financial results.
Goldman said the Wertheimers also bought 25 percent of Blades Technology Ltd from the IDB group for $47 million in IDB shares.
The highly profitable Iscar is the world's fourth-largest maker of carbide metal cutting tools for industry. It was founded by Stef Wertheimer, who serves as chairman. His son Eitan is president.
IDB, one of Israel's leading holding companies, is controlled by the Recanati family. Its 26.7 stake in Iscar was held by its subsidiary Discount Investments.

Discount said that as a result of the Iscar and Blades sale it would record an after-tax capital gain of $51 million in the third quarter of 1997. Discount said it planned to sell the shares in IDB to institutional and other long-term investors.
IDB and Discount are among Israel's blue chip stocks and the Iscar stake was one of the group's most lucrative holdings.
"We had a strategic agreement. Over time each company went in a different direction," Eitan Wertheimer told Reuters.
The Wertheimers objected to the publication of Iscar's financial results since the company is private. But IDB, as a public company, argued it needed to publish Iscar's profits.
"We were chased by competitors and our products were copied. We wanted to minimise the information that comes out to the competition. Discount needed to maximise this information," Wertheimer said.
The dispute came to a head when the Wertheimers purchased 15.6 percent of IDB's shares in an attempt to push IDB to sell its Iscar stake.
The Iscar and Blades deal will reduce the Wertheimers' stake in IDB to 2.5 percent.

The Wertheimers now own 100 percent of Iscar and 50 percent of Blades, a maker of aircraft propeller blades. The other half is held by jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a subsidiary of United Technologies Corp.
Iscar had sales last year of $330 million and 99 percent of its production was for export, Wertheimer said.
Eitan Wertheimer is also president of Blades and his father is chairman. The company had sales last year of $48.1 million, all of which was exported, according to Dun & Bradstreet.
